### 📓 Docs Drift Check
**1** anchor(s) derived from **1** changed package(s); no hand-written page names any of them, so this run has **nothing to list** — **not a clean bill of health**. This check sees only pages that NAME a derived anchor: one that documents this change in prose, or enumerates it in an authoring dialect, names none and stays invisible to it on every run.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- the SDK route bridge reached **60** of **216** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **156** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **156**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **55** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **101** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **35** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 2f7977cd2f25d878f31942dae6e229af9ff316d3` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

## Consumer acceptance (mobile shell side), head `b5658de9`

**Verdict: accepted with two should-fixes. Not mergeable until CI on the head is green.** At review time, Build & E2E UI, the only job that runs the new Playwright spec, was still in progress. The PR touches `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, so it is Tier H and a human merges it.

All five card items are met:
- the app-shell precache drops the old caches;
- no API responses are cached: `/api/`, cross-origin, out-of-scope and non-GET requests bypass the worker, and navigations are never stored;
- the update flow uses a network-first document with `skipWaiting` and `clients.claim`;
- `push` and `notificationclick` resolve `route` against the scope, which matches the shell's `consoleUrl`;
- the console is installable with default branding.

Nothing escapes the Console's same-origin scope.

### Should-fix (this PR)

**1. No test covers the native-shell guard.** `syncServiceWorker()` skips registration and unregisters any earlier worker when `getNativeHost()` is set (`ui/apps/console/src/main.tsx:229-233`). That one line protects the mobile shell's offline fallback, and the Verification section claims it, but no test exercises it. Suggested Playwright cases:
- an `addInitScript` defines `window.ObjectStackNative`, then the test asserts that `getRegistrations()` is empty;
- register a worker first, reload with the bridge defined, and assert that the worker is gone.

**2. Bridge detection is a single read and can lose a race on Android.**
- react-native-webview injects the bridge at `onPageStarted`, which can land after the Console's scripts. The shell's `docs/HYBRID-SHELL.md` (Known limits) asks the Console not to rely on one read.
- If the read loses, the worker registers inside the Android WebView. On the next offline cold start it serves the cached shell, so the WebView's `onError` never fires. The user then sees the Console's unreachable panel instead of the shell's Retry / Change server screen.
- iOS is unaffected: without App-Bound Domains, WKWebView has no `navigator.serviceWorker`.
- Cheap fix: re-check `getNativeHost()` after `whenActive(registration)` and unregister if it is now set.

### Follow-ups (not this PR)

- **Shared route rule.** The worker accepts dot segments that stay inside the scope, `%2f` / `%5c`, double encoding and C1 controls, all of which the shell's `safeConsoleRoute` refuses. At a root mount it also opens `/api/v1/...`. Share one rule with `PushRouteSchema` (see the should-fix on #29218).
- **Branded icon.** The manifest icon is hard-coded `image/svg+xml, sizes: any` (`main.tsx:176-181`), so a PNG favicon set in Setup is mis-declared and a branded Console may not be installable. This predates the PR; it is filed as a card.
- **Mobile side.** The shell's docs will state that the Console registers no Service Worker inside the shell, and why.

## Contract review

Served-tier: `TIER_DEFAULT`
Head-sha: `55e3e5e501fa69124b14cfa9e536b78fd5845afd`
Local-runs: none

Face: declaration, for the diff outside the governed hit. The PR body and the changeset declare `Clause-②: yes (widening)` (claim amended 6573560502). The one governed path, `.github/workflows/ci.yml`, owes its own `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` record from the director seat, which has been asked separately. This record covers the rest of the diff, as a standalone PR of those files would be reviewed.

### ① Derived judgments

- **`@object-ui/mobile` widens, and nothing narrows.**
  - `ServiceWorkerSourceOptions` gains the optional `strategy` (`'offline-first' | 'app-shell'`), `build` and `notifications`.
  - The entry gains `cacheLoadedResources`, `SERVICE_WORKER_CACHE_URLS_MESSAGE` and the type `ServiceWorkerStrategy`.
  - The default `'offline-first'` output is byte-identical to `main`, pinned by the generator suite, so every existing caller gets the same worker.
  
  Correct, and a widening.
- **API requests are network-only, as ruled.** The `'app-shell'` worker's fetch handler returns before `respondWith` for:
  - any non-GET request;
  - a URL under the API prefix;
  - another origin, or anything outside the worker's scope (`/_console/`).
  
  Such a request is never answered from, read from or written to the cache. Navigations are network-first and fall back to the cached shell. Hashed assets are cache-first.
- **No stale shell.** The cache name carries the build id, and activation deletes only this scope's older caches. Install calls `skipWaiting()`, so the next navigation after a deploy runs the new build. The e2e spec pins both offline reload and the update pickup.
- **No worker in native shell mode, as ruled.** `syncServiceWorker()` in `main.tsx` checks `getNativeHost()` first, and inside the mobile shell it unregisters a worker this Console registered earlier. It registers only in production builds, under the Console's own mount. It builds on #29140's shell detection, now on `main`.
- **The CSP widening is narrow.** `packages/cli/src/utils/console.ts` adds `manifest-src 'self' blob:` (option A, amendment 6573999866), pinned by its test. A `blob:` manifest can only be minted by a script that already passed `script-src`, and the stale comment that said `default-src` covered the manifest is corrected.
- **Notifications only route inside the app.** `notificationclick` opens or navigates only to a route that resolves inside the Console's scope. The worker does not subscribe to push.
- **The build plumbing is what the gates require.** These are the `tsconfig.node.json` include (6574807547) and the three `turbo.json` inputs (6575431847). Each is one line of the pattern already in those files for `ui/scripts/vite-*.ts`.
- **No new npm dependency.** The lockfile is untouched.

### ② Semver level

The changeset entries are `patch` for `@object-ui/mobile`, `@object-ui/console` and `@objectstack/cli`, with `Metadata-protocol: none`. AGENTS.md Post-Task Checklist step 3: a non-protocol change, widening or breaking, ships `patch`. Consistent.

### ③ Boundary flags

- **Tier H.** The `ci.yml` row (6575983994) makes the whole PR governed. The maintainer's decision is pending on the seat thread, and the seat will not flip ready or enqueue it before an authorized approval or a human merge.
- **Lint UI fixed.** The red on `b5658de9` was fixed inside the surface: an unused ESLint directive, and a doc snippet that read `process`. It is green on this head.
- The PR author is `objectstack-fleet[bot]`, so there is no off-relay writer to name.
